claims: For a discretely concave integer objective on a finite domain, a candidate that beats both local neighbors is a global maximum.
Right-neighbor failure and left-neighbor failure produce explicit better witnesses, so failed local certificates are not silently accepted.
Strict discrete concavity forces distinct maximizers to be adjacent.
The maximizer set of a discretely concave objective is interval-closed.
